#image("/imgs/ap-calc-ab-2021-frq-04-diagram-01.png", width: 65%)

Let $f$ be a continuous function defined on the closed interval $- 4 <= x <= 6$. The graph of $f$, consisting of four line segments, is shown above. Let $G$ be the function defined by $G(x)= integral_(0)^(x) f(t) d t$.

(a) On what open intervals is the graph of $G$ concave up? Give a reason for your answer.

(b) Let $P$ be the function defined by $P(x)= G(x) dot.c f(x)$. Find $P'(3)$.

(c) Find $lim_(x -> 2) frac(G(x),x^(2)- 2 x)$.

(d) Find the average rate of change of $G$ on the interval \[-4, 2\]. Does the Mean Value Theorem guarantee a value $c \,- 4 < c < 2$, for which $G'(c)$ is equal to this average rate of change? Justify your answer.
